title: Decision Ladder: Playback Journey for Canary Rollout Rehearsal
creator: Priya Shah
description: Design a lightweight ‘Decision Ladder’ playback view that lets SREs and PMs rehearse a canary rollout and staged rollback in the Console. The feature focuses on presenting an interactive timeline of signals, the decisions taken at each step, and a replay control to simulate changing traffic splits and trigger a rollback. The prototype will be used in usability sessions and as a reference for Eng and PM when defining rollout APIs and telemetry needs.
acceptance_criteria: Clickable prototype that demonstrates: (a) timeline scrub + play/pause; (b) toggling hypothetical signal injections (error spike, latency drift, cost variance); (c) simulated traffic split adjustments with immediate visualized impact; (d) a rollback ‘snapback’ control that animates moving traffic to fallback variant
Prototype screens annotated with required telemetry events (signal types, sample rates, decision markers) to hand off to ENG
Design spec includes accessibility considerations (contrast, keyboard scrubbing, screen reader labels) and copy for each state
Usability script and list of 6 tasks prepared for a 45-minute moderated session with PLG and SRE participants
Implementation Reno: an early engineering checklist with 5 required API hooks and an example mock payload for replay mode
comments: 2026-02-12 - PS: Kickoff sync with Marcus and Elena (PM). Outlined core scenarios: canary -> ramp -> anomaly -> rollback. Agreed to scope to single-run replay (no multi-variant branching) for v0.

2026-02-20 - ML: Early wireframes uploaded to Figma. Focus on a compact timeline with stacked signal lanes and decision markers. Need clarity on which signals are 'primary' vs 'secondary' for visual weighting.

2026-02-25 - MM (Marcus): Reviewed wireframes; engineering constraints: backend can emit sampled decision markers and a compact JSON for replay, but cannot stream full token-level traces. Adjusted prototype to use aggregated per-minute signals.

2026-03-02 - PS: Usability script drafted. Two tasks to validate: (1) detect anomaly and initiate rollback; (2) adjust traffic split to validate partial mitigation. Added success metrics (task completion, time to decision, confidence rating).

2026-03-05 - EE (Elena): Design review notes - clarify copy on rollback confirmation, add undo affordance, call out required telemetry: 'decision_id', 'signal_snapshot', 'traffic_split_before', 'traffic_split_after'.

2026-03-09 - PS: Mid-fidelity interactive prototype uploaded. Animations for scrub and rollback included. Shared with SRE for technical vetting. Marcus to coordinate engineering follow-up (ENG-89210 dependency).
2026-03-11 - MJ (design reviewer): Accessibility pass done; keyboard scrubbing added. Minor comment: legend colors should be colorblind-friendly; updated palette in Figma.

2026-03-12 - MM: Preparing PRD paragraph for the rollout API hooks (link to PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1024). Need to confirm event retention window for replay (recommendation: 72 hours).
notes_for_engineering: Prototype expects a replay endpoint that returns time-series buckets with: timestamp, metric_values (latency, err_rate, cost), active_decision (id, label), traffic_splits
Fallback variants should be addressable by stable variant_id; prototype uses ids: fallback_v1, canary_v2
Replay mode should be able to accept injected hypothetical signal deltas for testing (e.g., +50% latency)
Keep the first iteration client-side only (mocked data) to unblock usability testing; engineering to implement server-side replay in a follow-up story
